issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op (Stage I) asserts, with only a reference to a schematic figure, that each cutoff term h_k can be represented as A_k^out ∘ (ReLU∘A_k) ∘ ⋯ ∘ (ReLU∘A_1) with A_i, A_i^out ∈ aff_{≤5d} and the first k−1 layers shared and frozen across all grades. Each Γ_{Q_k} depends on x through a cube-specific affine shift c_k, yet the shared frozen layers must carry enough information about x for the k-th and later layers to compute later cutoffs. No explicit weight construction or proof of existence is provided; the figure description (d ReLU pass-through units plus 4d Ψ_k units per layer) is not justified and does not establish that the claimed width 5d suffices for the shared-layer structure.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a rigorous explicit construction of the affine maps A_i and A_i^out demonstrating that each h_k is realized by the stated k-layer ReLU composition with width 5d and shared frozen layers, or establish a corrected width bound and adjust the theorem statements accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The network realization step of Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op is missing, so the theorem is unproved. Theorem thm:main:mgdl and Corollary coro:mgdl:residual, which rely on thm:main:mgdl:one:op, are transitively unproved.
issues.title: Network realization with shared frozen layers asserted without proof
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained nontrivial construction (or a width correction), but no new global proof architecture is needed and the fixed-width multigrade convergence guarantee survives with a comparable width.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $f \in C([0,1]^d)$ be given. There exist $n\in\N^+$ and affine maps

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op allows any f ∈ C([0,1]^d) and claims strict decrease ‖f_{k+1}‖_{L^p} < ‖f_k‖_{L^p} for k = 1,…,n. When f = 0: f_1 = f = 0 gives ‖f_1‖_{L^p} = 0, so the inequality ‖f_2‖_{L^p} < 0 is impossible. The construction produces no cutoff terms (M_f = M_{−f} = 0), yielding f_k = 0 for all k and only non-strict equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis f ≠ 0 to Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op and handle f = 0 trivially in Theorem thm:main:mgdl, or weaken strict monotonicity to non-strict in the degenerate case.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op is false for f = 0. The proof of Theorem thm:main:mgdl and Corollary coro:mgdl:residual fails at the degenerate case (those results may still hold via a different construction with nonzero initial approximation).
issues.title: Strict L^p monotonicity is impossible when f = 0
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local nondegeneracy condition (f ≠ 0) or a degenerate-case bypass preserves every substantive claim and guarantee for nontrivial targets; f = 0 is trivially approximable.

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:dilated-cube-cutoff requires Γ_Q = 0 outside rQ, but the explicit formula Γ_Q(x) = Ψ((2/ℓ(Q))(x − c(Q))) with Ψ(x) = (1/d)Σψ(x_i) does not satisfy this: when one normalized coordinate exceeds r (so x ∉ rQ) the corresponding ψ vanishes but the remaining d−1 terms can be positive, giving Γ_Q(x) > 0. The proof of condition (C1) in Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:contraction uses the false step Γ_{Q_i}(x) = 0 outside ⋃rQ_i to conclude T_ε g(x) = 0 there and hence T_ε g ≤ g^+. With the sum-based formula, T_ε g can exceed g^+ at points outside the dilated cubes (e.g., where g vanishes but the average of ψ is positive), violating the pointwise bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Ψ(x) = (1/d)Σψ(x_i) with a valid d-dimensional cutoff that vanishes outside [−r,r]^d, e.g., Ψ(x) = min_{1≤i≤d} ψ(x_i). The proof of Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:constraction works unchanged with any valid cutoff satisfying the three stated properties.
issues.overall_effect: The positive ε-contraction property of T_ε (Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:constraction) is unproved, breaking the balanced-contraction argument in Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op and the entire proof chain for Theorem thm:main:mgdl and Corollary coro:mgdl:residual.
issues.title: Cutoff function with sum-of-psi formula does not vanish outside rQ
issues.why_classification: Changing the formula to a valid cutoff (e.g., using min instead of the average) is a short, local repair that preserves Lemma lem:T:positive:eps:constraction and its proof without any new lemma, construction, or replacement argument.
